main.description: The universal 'X authorizes/trusts Y to act in some capacity' primitive — one record for what used to be role_grant, patron delegates, and charter-named arbiters/witnesses/labelers. A grantor designates a `grantee` DID for a `capability`, within a `scope`, optionally time-boxed (`expiry`) and chained (`prev`). Two modes: 'delegate' = the grantee may act WITH the grantor's authority (attenuated, revocable, chainable — UCAN-style; their records in scope count as authorized by the grantor); 'trust' = the grantor RELIES ON the grantee for a function (arbiter/witness/labeler) with no authority transfer. Authorized iff the grantor either owns the resource in scope or holds an upstream designation/charter capability that includes granting it, and (for delegate) the capability+scope are a subset of the parent's (attenuation). Where the capability requires the designee's consent (e.g. taking an officer or arbiter role), they co-sign with org.buildguild.acceptance. Revoked by deleting/superseding this record (the grantor owns it; the deletion is witnessed like any other). Author is the grantor (repo owner). Written to the grantor's repo.

mode.description: 'delegate' = act WITH the grantor's authority (attenuated, revocable, chainable); 'trust' = the grantor relies on the grantee for the capability, no authority transfer.

capability.description: What the grantee may do / is trusted for — an id from the capability ontology, e.g. 'quest.transact', 'role:officer', 'guild.admit', 'dispute.arbitrate', 'delivery.witness', 'moderation.label'.

scope.description: What it applies to: an AT-URI / guild id / quest strongRef-uri, or '*' for all the grantor's resources. Attenuation lives here — a sub-delegation's scope must be within the parent's.

prev.description: Optional parent designation this one chains from (UCAN-style). Lets an authorized holder sub-delegate an attenuated capability — enabling nested enterprises (guild-of-guilds, per-quest sub-parties).

expiry.description: Optional expiry; after this the designation no longer counts (time-boxed authority/trust).

reason.description: Optional human note — part of the public trail.
